1-1: To learn and, in season, to practise what you have learned — is that not a pleasure?
1-2: 其為人也孝弟，而好犯上者，鮮矣；不好犯上，而……
Those who are filial and fraternal yet fond of defying their superiors are few; those not fond of defying their superiors yet fond of starting disorder have never existed.
1-3: 吾日三省吾身：為人謀而不忠乎
Each day I examine myself on three counts. In acting for others, have I been less than wholehearted?
1-4: 道千乘之國：敬事而信，節用而愛人，使民以時
To govern a state of a thousand chariots: be careful in affairs and keep faith; be sparing in expense and love the people; and call on the people's labour only in the right season.
1-5: 賢賢易色，事父母能竭其力，事君能致其身，與朋……

One who values his wife for her character rather than her looks, serves his parents with all his strength, serves his ruler with his whole person, and keeps his word with friends — though people say he has not studied, I would certainly say he has.
1-6: 君子不重則不威，學則不固
If a gentleman lacks weight he will have no dignity, and what he learns will not hold firm.
1-7: Take care over the end, and follow the distant dead with remembrance, and the people's virtue will return to fullness.
1-8: 子禽問於子貢曰：夫子至於是邦也，必聞其政，求……
Ziqin asked Zigong: Whenever the Master arrives in a state he always hears about its government. Does he seek this, or is it given to him?
1-9: 父在，觀其志；父沒，觀其行；三年無改於父之道……
While his father lives, observe his intentions; after his father dies, observe his conduct. If for three years he makes no change to his father's way, he may be called filial.
1-10: In the practice of ritual, harmony is what is prized.
1-11: 信近於義，言可復也；恭近於禮，遠恥辱也；因不……

When a promise comes close to what is right, one's word can be kept. When respect comes close to ritual, one keeps shame and disgrace away. When one relies on those one has not lost closeness with, one can look up to them.
1-12: 君子食無求飽，居無求安，敏於事而慎於言，就有……
A gentleman does not seek to eat his fill or live in comfort; he is quick in action and careful in speech, and goes to those who have the Way to be set straight. He may be called fond of learning.
1-13: 貧而無諂，富而無驕，何如
Poor without flattery, rich without arrogance — how is that?
1-14: 不患人之不己知，患不知人也
Do not be troubled that others do not know you; be troubled that you do not know others.
1-15: 為政以德，譬如北辰，居其所而眾星共之
One who governs by virtue is like the pole star: it stays in its place, and all the other stars turn toward it.
1-16: 道之以政，齊之以刑，民免而無恥；道之以德，齊……

Guide them by decrees and keep them in line by punishments, and the people will stay out of trouble but have no sense of shame. Guide them by virtue and keep them in line by ritual, and they will have a sense of shame and, moreover, come right.
1-17: 吾十有五而志於學，三十而立，四十而不惑，五十……

At fifteen I set my heart on learning; at thirty I stood firm; at forty I had no doubts; at fifty I knew the decree of Heaven; at sixty my ear was attuned; at seventy I could follow my heart's desire without overstepping the line.
1-18: Meng Yizi asked about filial piety. The Master said: Do not go against it.
1-19: 孟武伯問孝。子曰：父母唯其疾之憂
Meng Wubo asked about filial piety. The Master said: Parents worry only about their children falling ill.
1-20: Zixia asked about filial piety. The Master said: The face is the hard part.
1-21: 吾與回言終日，不違如愚
I talked with Hui all day and he never disagreed, as if he were slow.
1-22: 溫故而知新，可以為師矣
One who reviews the old and comes to know the new may be a teacher.
1-23: 子貢問君子。子曰：先行其言而後從之
Zigong asked about the gentleman. The Master said: He first acts on his words, and then speaks of them.
1-24: 學而不思則罔，思而不學則殆
To learn without thinking is to be lost; to think without learning is perilous.
1-25: To bore into one end of a matter only — that is harmful indeed.
1-26: You, shall I teach you about knowing?
1-27: 子張學干祿。子曰：多聞闕疑，慎言其餘，則寡尤……
Zizhang was studying in order to gain office. The Master said: Hear much, set aside what is doubtful, and speak carefully of the rest — then you will make few mistakes…
1-28: 何為則民服？孔子對曰：舉直錯諸枉，則民服；舉……
What should I do so that the people will submit? Confucius replied: Raise up the straight and set them over the crooked, and the people will submit; raise up…
1-29: 臨之以莊則敬，孝慈則忠，舉善而教不能則勸
Approach them with dignity and they will be respectful; be filial and kind and they will be loyal; raise up the good and teach those who are not able, and they will be eager.
1-30: 或謂孔子曰：子奚不為政
Someone said to Confucius: Why do you not take part in government?
1-31: A person without trustworthiness — I do not know how he can manage.
2-1: 殷因於夏禮，所損益，可知也；周因於殷禮，所損……
Yin followed the rites of Xia; what it took away and added can be known. Zhou followed the rites of Yin; what it took away…
2-2: To sacrifice to spirits not one's own is flattery.
2-3: 孔子謂季氏：八佾舞於庭，是可忍也，孰不可忍也
Confucius said of the Ji family: Eight rows of dancers in his courtyard — if he can bear to do this, what can he not bear to do?
2-4: Lin Fang asked about the root of ritual.
2-5: 夷狄之有君，不如諸夏之亡也
The Yi and Di with rulers are not like the Xia states without them.
2-6: The gentleman does not compete — except, perhaps, in archery!
2-7: 巧笑倩兮，美目盼兮，素以為絢兮
Her artful smile dimpling, her lovely eyes clear, white to set off the colours.
2-8: 夏禮吾能言之，杞不足徵也；殷禮吾能言之，宋不……
I can speak of the rites of Xia, but Qi cannot bear them out; I can speak of the rites of Yin, but Song cannot…
2-9: 禘自既灌而往者，吾不欲觀之矣
At the di sacrifice, from the libation onwards, I do not wish to watch.
2-10: Sacrifice as if they were present; sacrifice to the spirits as if the spirits were present.
2-11: 周監於二代，郁郁乎文哉
Zhou looked to the two dynasties before it — how rich and refined its culture!
2-12: 射不主皮，為力不同科，古之道也
In archery, piercing the hide is not the point, because men's strength is not of the same grade. That was the way of old.
2-13: Serving one's lord with full ritual, people take it for flattery.
2-14: The Guanju — joyful but not excessive, sorrowful but not hurtful.
2-15: Duke Ai asked Zai Wo about the altar of the soil.
2-16: Guan Zhong's capacity was small indeed!
2-17: The Master spoke of music to the Grand Music Master of Lu.
2-18: 儀封人請見。曰：君子之至於斯也，吾未嘗不得見……
The border warden of Yi asked to be presented, saying: Whenever a gentleman comes here, I have never failed to see him…
2-19: 子謂韶，盡美矣，又盡善也
The Master said of the Shao: Perfectly beautiful, and perfectly good.
2-20: 里仁為美。擇不處仁，焉得知
It is beautiful to live where humaneness prevails. If one chooses not to dwell among the humane, how can one be called wise?
2-21: Only the humane can love others and can hate others.
2-22: 富與貴是人之所欲也，不以其道得之，不處也；貧……
Wealth and rank are what people want; if not obtained by the proper way, one does not keep them. Poverty…
2-23: 我未見好仁者，惡不仁者
I have not seen one who loves humaneness or one who hates what is not humane.
2-24: People's faults each belong to their kind.
2-25: If one hears the Way in the morning, one may die at dusk without regret.
2-26: 士志於道，而恥惡衣惡食者，未足與議也
A scholar who sets his heart on the Way, yet is ashamed of poor clothes and poor food, is not worth talking with.
2-27: 君子懷德，小人懷土；君子懷刑，小人懷惠
The gentleman cherishes virtue, the petty man cherishes his own ground; the gentleman cherishes the law, the petty man cherishes favors.
2-28: Can one govern a state with ritual and yielding?
3-1: 君子喻於義，小人喻於利
The gentleman understands rightness; the small man understands profit.
3-2: 見賢思齊焉，見不賢而內自省也
Seeing a worthy person, think of equalling him; seeing an unworthy one, turn inward and examine yourself.
3-3: While your parents are alive, do not travel far.
3-4: The ages of one's parents must not go unknown.
3-5: 君子欲訥於言而敏於行
The gentleman wishes to be slow in speech and quick in action.
3-6: Virtue is not solitary; it is sure to have neighbours.
3-7: 事君數，斯辱矣，朋友數，斯疏矣
In serving a ruler, importunity brings disgrace; among friends, importunity brings distance.
3-8: The Master said of Gongye Chang: He is fit to be given a wife.
3-9: The Master said of Zijian: A gentleman indeed is this man!
3-10: Yong is humane but not glib.
3-11: If the Way does not prevail, I will board a raft and float out to sea.
3-12: 不知也。又問。子曰：由也，千乘之國，可使治其……
I do not know. He asked again. The Master said: You could be put in charge of the levies of a state of a thousand chariots; I do not know whether he is humane.
3-13: 子謂子貢曰：女與回也孰愈
The Master said to Zigong: Who is better, you or Hui?
3-14: 宰予晝寢。子曰：朽木不可雕也，糞土之牆不可杇……
Zai Yu slept in the daytime. The Master said: Rotten wood cannot be carved; a wall of dung cannot be plastered. As for Yu, what is the use of scolding him?
3-15: 吾未見剛者。或對曰：申棖
I have never seen anyone who is truly firm. Someone answered: Shen Cheng.
3-16: 夫子之文章，可得而聞也；夫子之言性與天道，不……
The Master's outward cultivation we may hear about; the Master's words on human nature and the Way of Heaven we may not hear about.
3-18: 子謂子產，有君子之道四焉：其行己也恭，其事上……

The Master said of Zichan: He had four ways of the gentleman. In conducting himself he was respectful; in serving his superiors he was reverent; in nourishing the people he was kind; in employing the people he was just.
3-19: 晏平仲善與人交，久而敬之
Yan Pingzhong was good at associating with others; long acquainted, he still treated them with respect.
3-20: 令尹子文三仕為令尹，無喜色；三已之，無慍色
Prime Minister Ziwen took office as prime minister three times without a look of joy, and was dismissed three times without a look of resentment.
3-21: Ji Wenzi thought three times before he acted.
3-22: 歸與！歸與！吾黨之小子狂簡，斐然成章，不知所……
Let us go home! Let us go home! The young men of my village are ambitious and careless; they have produced something of real pattern, but do not know how to cut it to shape.
3-23: 伯夷、叔齊不念舊惡，怨是用希
Bo Yi and Shu Qi did not keep old wrongs in mind, and so resentment was rare.
3-24: 巧言、令色、足恭，左丘明恥之，丘亦恥之
Fine words, an ingratiating face, excessive deference — Zuoqiu Ming was ashamed of them, and I too am ashamed of them.
3-25: 顏淵、季路侍。子曰：盍各言爾志
Yan Yuan and Ji Lu were attending. The Master said: Why not each tell me your wishes?
3-26: 已矣乎！吾未見能見其過而內自訟者也
It is hopeless! I have yet to see anyone who can see his own faults and bring the charge against himself inwardly.
3-27: Yong could be given the seat facing south.
3-28: 有顏回者好學，不遷怒，不貳過
There was Yan Hui who loved learning. He did not shift his anger, and did not repeat a fault.
3-29: 子華使於齊，冉子為其母請粟
Zihua was sent on a mission to Qi, and Ranzi asked for grain for his mother.
3-30: 子謂仲弓曰：犁牛之子騂且角，雖欲勿用，山川其……
The Master, speaking of Zhonggong, said: If the calf of a brindled ox is red and well-horned, even if people would rather not use it, would the spirits of the hills and rivers reject it?
3-31: You is decisive; what difficulty would he have in government?
4-1: The Ji family wanted to make Min Ziqian steward of Bi.
4-2: 伯牛有疾，子問之，自牖執其手，曰：亡之，命矣……
Boniu was ill. The Master went to ask after him, and holding his hand through the window, said: We are losing him; it is fate!
4-3: 賢哉，回也！一簞食，一瓢飲，在陋巷
How worthy Hui is! A bamboo basket of rice, a gourd of water, living in a mean alley.
4-4: 非不說子之道，力不足也
It is not that I do not delight in your Way, Master; my strength is not enough.
4-6: Meng Zhifan does not boast. When the army fled, he guarded the rear.
4-7: 不有祝鮀之佞而有宋朝之美，難乎免於今之世矣
Without the glibness of the priest Tuo, but with the beauty of Song Zhao, it is hard to escape harm in today's world!
4-8: 人之生也直，罔之生也幸而免
Man lives by uprightness; the crooked live only by luck, having escaped.
4-9: 知之者不如好之者，好之者不如樂之者
Those who know it are not equal to those who love it; those who love it are not equal to those who delight in it.
4-10: 中人以上，可以語上也；中人以下，不可以語上也
To those above the middling, one can speak of higher things; to those below the middling, one cannot speak of higher things.
4-11: 樊遲問知。子曰：務民之義，敬鬼神而遠之，可謂……
Fan Chi asked about wisdom. The Master said: To devote oneself to what is right for the people, and to revere the spirits while keeping them at a distance, may be called wisdom.
4-12: 知者樂水，仁者樂山；知者動，仁者靜；知者樂，……
The wise delight in water; the humane delight in mountains. The wise are active; the humane are still. The wise are joyful; the humane live long.
4-13: 仁者，雖告之曰：井有仁焉
If a humane man were told, 'Someone humane has fallen into the well,'
4-14: 君子博學於文，約之以禮，亦可以弗畔矣夫
A gentleman who learns broadly in culture and restrains it with ritual may thereby avoid going astray.
4-15: The Master went to see Nanzi, and Zilu was displeased.
4-16: 如有博施於民而能濟眾，何如
If someone gave widely to the people and could relieve the multitude, what would you say?
4-17: 述而不作，信而好古，竊比於我老彭
I transmit and do not create; I trust and love antiquity. I venture to compare myself to our Old Peng.
4-18: 德之不修，學之不講，聞義不能徙，不善不能改，……
Virtue not cultivated, learning not discussed, hearing what is right yet not moving toward it, having faults yet not correcting them — these are my worries.
4-19: 志於道，據於德，依於仁，遊於藝
Set your will on the Way, hold to virtue, rely on humaneness, and roam in the arts.
4-20: I do not open the way for one who is not eager, nor help out one who is not struggling to speak.
4-21: 子謂顏淵曰：用之則行，舍之則藏；唯我與爾有是……
The Master said to Yan Yuan: When employed, act; when set aside, withdraw — only you and I are like this.
4-22: 富而可求也，雖執鞭之士，吾亦為之
If wealth could be sought, I would do it even as a man holding the whip.
4-23: The things the Master was careful about: fasting, war, and illness.
4-24: Is our Master on the side of the ruler of Wei?
4-25: 飯疏食飲水，曲肱而枕之，樂亦在其中矣
Eating coarse food and drinking water, bending my arm for a pillow — there is joy in this too.
4-26: 加我數年，五十以學易，可以無大過矣
Give me a few more years, and if I could study the Changes at fifty, I might be free of great faults.
4-27: 葉公問孔子於子路，子路不對
The Duke of She asked Zilu about Confucius, and Zilu did not answer.
4-28: The Master did not speak of the strange, of force, of disorder, or of spirits.
4-29: When three walk together, there is surely a teacher for me among them.
4-30: 天生德於予，桓魋其如予何
Heaven gave birth to the virtue in me; what can Huan Tui do to me?
5-1: 聖人，吾不得而見之矣；得見君子者，斯可矣
A sage I cannot hope to see; if I could see a gentleman, that would be enough.
5-2: The Master fished with a line but not with a net; he shot birds with a corded arrow, but not birds at roost.
5-3: 仁遠乎哉？我欲仁，斯仁至矣
Is humaneness far away? I wish for humaneness, and here humaneness is.
5-4: 知禮。孔子退，揖巫馬期而進之，曰：吾聞君子不……
He knew ritual. After Confucius withdrew, the minister bowed Wuma Qi forward and said: I have heard that a gentleman is not partial; is a gentleman partial after all?
5-5: 子與人歌而善，必使反之，而後和之
When the Master sang with others and someone sang well, he would have him repeat it, and then join in.
5-6: As for sagehood and humaneness, how would I dare?
5-7: The Master was gravely ill, and Zilu asked to offer prayers.
5-8: 君子坦蕩蕩，小人長慼慼
The gentleman is open and at ease; the petty man is always anxious and distressed.
5-9: 子溫而厲，威而不猛，恭而安
The Master was gentle yet stern, commanding yet not fierce, respectful yet at ease.
5-10: 泰伯，其可謂至德也已矣
Taibo may be called a man of the highest virtue!
5-11: 恭而無禮則勞，慎而無禮則葸，勇而無禮則亂，直……
Respect without ritual becomes toil; caution without ritual becomes timidity; courage without ritual becomes disorder; straightness without ritual becomes harshness.
5-12: 曾子有疾，召門弟子曰：啟予足
Zengzi was ill and called his disciples: Uncover my feet!
5-13: Zengzi was ill and Meng Jingzi came to ask after him.
5-14: 以能問於不能，以多問於寡；有若無，實若虛；犯……
Able, yet asking those less able; knowing much, yet asking those who know little; having, as if not having; full, as if empty; wronged, yet not retaliating.
5-15: 可以託六尺之孤，可以寄百里之命，臨大節而不可……
One who can be entrusted with an orphaned young ruler, who can be given charge of a state of a hundred li, and who in a great crisis cannot be swayed
5-16: 士不可以不弘毅，任重而道遠
A scholar must be broad and resolute, for his burden is heavy and his road is long.
5-17: 民可使由之，不可使知之
The people can be made to follow it, but cannot be made to understand it.
5-18: 如有周公之才之美，使驕且吝，其餘不足觀也已
Even with the talents and fine qualities of the Duke of Zhou, if a man were arrogant and stingy, the rest would not be worth looking at.
5-19: Hold firmly to good faith and love learning; guard the good Way unto death.
5-20: When not in the office, do not plan its affairs.
5-21: Learn as if you could not catch up, and still fear losing it.
5-22: Great indeed was Yao as a ruler!
5-23: Shun had five ministers and the realm was well governed.
5-24: In Yu I find no fault.
5-25: The Master seldom spoke of profit, but he endorsed fate and endorsed humaneness.
5-26: 子絕四：毋意，毋必，毋固，毋我
The Master was free of four things: no presumption, no insistence, no stubbornness, no self.
5-27: 子畏於匡。曰：文王既沒，文不在茲乎
The Master was in peril in Kuang. He said: Since King Wen is gone, is culture not here in me?
5-28: 大宰問於子貢曰：夫子聖者與
The Grand Steward asked Zigong: Is your Master a sage?
5-29: Do I have knowledge? I do not.
5-30: 鳳鳥不至，河不出圖，吾已矣夫
The phoenix does not come, the River gives forth no chart. It is all over with me!
5-31: 顏淵喟然嘆曰：仰之彌高，鑽之彌堅；瞻之在前，……
Yan Yuan sighed deeply and said: The more I look up to it, the higher it is; the more I bore into it, the harder it is. I see it before me, and suddenly it is behind.
6-1: 子疾病，子路使門人為臣
The Master was gravely ill, and Zilu had disciples act as his retainers.
6-2: 有美玉於斯，韞匵而藏諸
Here is a beautiful jade. Should one store it away in a case?
6-3: 子欲居九夷。或曰：陋，如之何
The Master wished to live among the nine Yi tribes. Someone said: They are crude; what would you do?
6-4: 出則事公卿，入則事父兄，喪事不敢不勉，不為酒……
Abroad, serving dukes and ministers; at home, serving father and elder brothers; in mourning, never daring not to do my utmost; never being overcome by wine — which of these is in me?
6-5: 子在川上，曰：逝者如斯夫
Standing by a river, the Master said: It flows on like this!
6-6: 吾未見好德如好色者也
I have never seen anyone who loves virtue as much as he loves beauty.
6-7: 語之而不惰者，其回也與
One who never grew lax when I spoke to him — that was Hui!
6-8: 後生可畏，焉知來者之不如今也
The young are to be held in awe. How do we know those to come will not equal those of today?
6-9: Words of correction — can one fail to accept them?
6-10: 主忠信，毋友不如己者，過則勿憚改
Hold loyalty and good faith as primary. Do not befriend those not your equal. When you err, do not fear to correct it.
6-11: 三軍可奪帥也，匹夫不可奪志也
The three armies can be robbed of their commander; a common man cannot be robbed of his will.
6-12: 衣敝縕袍，與衣狐貉者立，而不恥者，其由也與
Wearing a tattered padded robe and standing beside men in fox and badger furs without shame — that would be You, would it not?
6-13: 歲寒，然後知松柏之後彫也
Only when the year turns cold do we know that the pine and cypress are the last to wither.
6-14: 知者不惑，仁者不憂，勇者不懼
The wise are not perplexed; the humane are not anxious; the brave are not afraid.
6-15: 'The blossoms of the cherry tree flutter and turn.'
6-16: 孔子於鄉黨，恂恂如也，似不能言者
In his home village, Confucius was simple and sincere, as if unable to speak.
6-17: 朝，與下大夫言，侃侃如也；與上大夫言，誾誾如……
At court, speaking with lower officers, he was direct and at ease; speaking with higher officers, he was respectful and exact.
6-18: 君召使擯，色勃如也，足躩如也
When the ruler summoned him to receive guests, his face would change and his steps would quicken.
6-19: 入公門，鞠躬如也，如不容
Entering the palace gate, he bowed as if there were no room for him.
6-20: Holding the jade tablet, he bowed as if it were too heavy to bear.
6-21: The gentleman did not use dark purple or puce for trimmings.
6-22: When fasting, he always had a clean garment of plain cloth.
6-23: He did not tire of finely polished rice or of finely sliced meat.
6-24: If the mat was not straight, he did not sit.
6-25: The stables burned down. Returning from court, the Master said: Was anyone hurt?
6-26: 君賜食，必正席先嘗之；君賜腥，必熟而薦之；君……
When the ruler gave him cooked food, he would straighten his mat and taste it first. When the ruler gave him raw meat, he would cook it and offer it to his ancestors.
6-27: When a friend died, there was no one to take charge.
6-28: He did not sleep stretched out like a corpse, nor sit at home with formal bearing.
6-29: Mounting his carriage, he always stood upright and held the strap.
6-30: 先進於禮樂，野人也；後進於禮樂，君子也
Those who first advanced in ritual and music were country folk; those who later advanced in ritual and music were gentlemen.
7-1: 從我於陳、蔡者，皆不及門也
Those who followed me in Chen and Cai are no longer at my gate.
7-2: 回也非助我者也，於吾言無所不說
Hui is no help to me; there is nothing I say that he is not pleased with.
7-3: 南容三復白圭，孔子以其兄之子妻之
Nan Rong repeated the lines on the white jade tablet three times a day, and Confucius gave him his elder brother's daughter as wife.
7-4: 顏淵死，顏路請子之車以為之槨
When Yan Yuan died, Yan Lu asked for the Master's carriage to make an outer coffin for him.
7-5: When Yan Yuan died, the Master said: Alas!
7-6: 顏淵死，門人欲厚葬之，子曰：不可
When Yan Yuan died, the disciples wanted to give him a lavish burial. The Master said: No.
7-7: Jilu asked about serving the spirits.
7-8: 閔子侍側，誾誾如也；子路，行行如也；冉有、子……
Min Ziqian stood beside the Master, respectful and exact; Zilu, bold and firm; Ran You and Zigong, direct and at ease.
7-9: 魯人為長府。閔子騫曰：仍舊貫，如之何
The people of Lu were rebuilding the Long Treasury. Min Ziqian said: Why not keep it as it was?
7-10: What is You's zither doing at my gate?
7-11: Shi goes too far; Shang does not go far enough.
7-12: 季氏富於周公，而求也為之聚斂而附益之
The Ji family was richer than the Duke of Zhou, yet Qiu collected taxes for them and added to their wealth.
7-13: 柴也愚，參也魯，師也辟，由也喭
Chai is simple, Shen is slow, Shi is showy, You is coarse.
7-14: Zizhang asked about the way of the good man.
7-15: 有父兄在，如之何其聞斯行之
While your father and elder brothers are alive, how can you act at once on what you hear?
7-16: The Master was in peril in Kuang, and Yan Yuan fell behind.
7-17: 吾以子為異之問，曾由與求之問
I thought you would ask about someone remarkable, but you ask about You and Qiu.
7-18: Zilu had Zigao made steward of Bi.
7-19: 子路、曾皙、冉有、公西華侍坐
Zilu, Zeng Xi, Ran You, and Gongxi Hua sat in attendance.
7-20: 顏淵問仁。子曰：克己復禮為仁
Yan Yuan asked about humaneness. The Master said: To restrain oneself and return to ritual is humaneness.
7-21: 仲弓問仁。子曰：出門如見大賓，使民如承大祭
Zhonggong asked about humaneness. The Master said: Going out the gate, act as if receiving an honored guest; employing the people, act as if conducting a great sacrifice.
7-22: 司馬牛問仁。子曰：仁者其言也訒
Sima Niu asked about humaneness. The Master said: The humane are slow to speak.
7-23: Sima Niu asked about the gentleman.
7-24: 司馬牛憂曰：人皆有兄弟，我獨亡
Sima Niu said sorrowfully: Everyone has brothers; I alone have none.
7-25: 子張問明。子曰：浸潤之譖，膚受之愬，不行焉；……
Zizhang asked about clear-sightedness. The Master said: One on whom slander that seeps in slowly and complaints that cut to the skin have no effect…
7-26: Zigong asked about government. The Master said: Enough food.
7-27: 君子質而已矣，何以文為
A gentleman is substance, that is all; what need is there for refinement?
7-28: 哀公問於有若曰：年飢，用不足，如之何
Duke Ai asked You Ruo: The harvest is poor and there is not enough for expenses. What should be done?
7-29: Zizhang asked about exalting virtue and discerning delusion.
7-30: Duke Jing of Qi asked Confucius about government.
7-31: 片言可以折獄者，其由也與
One who could settle a lawsuit with half a word — that would be You, would it not?
8-1: 子張問政。子曰：居之無倦，行之以忠
Zizhang asked about government. The Master said: Hold your post without weariness, and carry it out with loyalty.
8-2: 君子成人之美，不成人之惡
The gentleman helps others achieve what is good in them, not what is bad.
8-3: Ji Kangzi asked Confucius about government.
8-4: 季康子問政於孔子曰：如殺無道，以就有道，何如
Ji Kangzi asked Confucius about government: What if I killed those without the Way in order to bring about the Way?
8-5: What do you mean by accomplished?
8-6: 樊遲從遊於舞雩之下，曰：敢問崇德、修慝、辨惑
Fan Chi was walking with the Master below the rain altar and said: May I ask about exalting virtue, rooting out hidden faults, and discerning delusion?
8-7: Fan Chi asked about humaneness. The Master said: Love others.
8-8: 君子以文會友，以友輔仁
The gentleman gathers friends through culture, and through friends supports his humaneness.
8-9: 子路問政。子曰：先之，勞之
Zilu asked about government. The Master said: Go before the people and work hard for them.
8-10: 衛君待子而為政，子將奚先
The ruler of Wei is waiting for you to govern. What will you do first?
8-11: 樊遲請學稼，子曰：吾不如老農
Fan Chi asked to learn farming. The Master said: I am not as good as an old farmer.
8-12: 其身正，不令而行；其身不正，雖令不從
If he himself is correct, things are done without orders; if he himself is not correct, even with orders they are not obeyed.
8-13: The governments of Lu and Wei are brothers.
8-14: The Master went to Wei, with Ran You driving.
8-15: 苟有用我者，期月而已可也，三年有成
If anyone would employ me, within a year things would be in fair shape, and in three years there would be results.
8-16: Even with a true king, it would take a generation for humaneness to prevail.
8-17: Ran Zi returned from court. The Master said: Why so late?
8-18: A saying cannot be expected to do that much.
8-19: Zixia, as steward of Jufu, asked about government.
8-20: 葉公語孔子曰：吾黨有直躬者，其父攘羊，而子證……
The Duke of She said to Confucius: In my village there is an upright man. When his father stole a sheep, the son bore witness against him…
8-21: 樊遲問仁。子曰：居處恭，執事敬，與人忠
Fan Chi asked about humaneness. The Master said: Be respectful at home, reverent in handling affairs, loyal in dealing with others.
8-22: What must one be like to be called a scholar?
8-23: 不得中行而與之，必也狂狷乎
If I cannot find those who walk the middle way to associate with, then I must have the ardent and the cautious!
8-24: 南人有言曰：人而無恆，不可以作巫醫
The southerners have a saying: 'A man without constancy cannot even be a shaman or a doctor.'
8-25: 君子和而不同，小人同而不和
The gentleman is harmonious but does not conform; the petty man conforms but is not harmonious.
8-26: What if everyone in the village likes him?
8-27: 君子易事而難說也：說之不以道，不說也；及其使……
The gentleman is easy to serve but hard to please. Try to please him by other than the Way, and he is not pleased; when he employs…
8-28: 君子泰而不驕，小人驕而不泰
The gentleman is at ease but not arrogant; the petty man is arrogant but not at ease.
8-29: What must one be like to be called a scholar?
8-30: 善人教民七年，亦可以即戎矣
When a good man has taught the people for seven years, they too can be sent to war.
8-31: 憲問恥。子曰：邦有道，穀；邦無道，穀，恥也
Xian asked about shame. The Master said: When the state has the Way, to draw a salary; when the state lacks the Way, to draw a salary — that is shameful.
9-1: 士而懷居，不足以為士矣
A scholar who cherishes his comfort is not worthy to be called a scholar.
9-2: 有德者必有言，有言者不必有德；仁者必有勇，勇……
Those with virtue are sure to have words worth hearing; those with words are not necessarily virtuous. The humane are sure to have courage; the courageous are not necessarily humane.
9-3: 南宮适問於孔子曰：羿善射，奡盪舟，俱不得其死……
Nangong Kuo asked Confucius: Yi was a fine archer and Ao could push a boat over land, yet neither died a natural death…
9-4: 君子而不仁者有矣夫，未有小人而仁者也
There may be gentlemen who are not humane, but there has never been a petty man who is humane.
9-5: 為命：裨諶草創之，世叔討論之，行人子羽修飾之……
In drafting state documents, Pi Chen made the first draft, Shishu examined and discussed it, the envoy Ziyu revised and polished it…
9-6: Someone asked about Zichan. The Master said: A kind man.
9-7: 貧而無怨難，富而無驕易
To be poor without resentment is hard; to be rich without arrogance is easy.
9-8: 子路問成人。子曰：若臧武仲之知，公綽之不欲，……
Zilu asked about the complete man. The Master said: One with the wisdom of Zang Wuzhong, the freedom from desire of Gongchuo…
9-9: 子問公叔文子於公明賈曰：信乎，夫子不言、不笑……
The Master asked Gongming Jia about Gongshu Wenzi: Is it true that your master does not speak, does not laugh, and does not take?
9-10: 臧武仲以防求為後於魯，雖曰不要君，吾不信也
Zang Wuzhong held on to Fang and demanded that an heir be appointed for him in Lu. Though he says he was not coercing his ruler, I do not believe it.
9-11: 桓公殺公子糾，召忽死之，管仲不死
Duke Huan had Prince Jiu killed. Shao Hu died with him, but Guan Zhong did not.
9-13: 公叔文子之臣大夫僎，與文子同升諸公
Zhuan, a household officer of Gongshu Wenzi, rose together with Wenzi to the ducal court.
9-14: 子言衛靈公之無道也，康子曰：夫如是，奚而不喪
The Master spoke of Duke Ling of Wei's lack of the Way. Ji Kangzi said: If he is like that, why has he not lost his state?
9-16: The gentleman reaches upward; the petty man reaches downward.
9-17: Qu Boyu sent a messenger to Confucius.
9-18: When not in the office, do not plan its affairs.
9-19: 君子道者三，我無能焉：仁者不憂，知者不惑，勇……
The way of the gentleman has three parts, and I have achieved none of them: the humane do not worry, the wise are not perplexed, the brave do not fear.
9-20: 不患人之不己知，患其不能也
Do not worry that others do not know you; worry that you lack ability.
9-21: 微生畝謂孔子曰：丘，何為是棲棲者與
Weisheng Mu said to Confucius: Qiu, why are you always so busily on the move?
9-22: What about repaying injury with kindness?
9-23: 莫我知也夫！子貢曰：何為其莫知子也
No one knows me! Zigong said: Why does no one know you?
9-24: Gongbo Liao slandered Zilu to Jisun.
9-25: 賢者辟世，其次辟地，其次辟色，其次辟言
The worthy withdraw from the world; the next withdraw from a place; the next withdraw at a look; the next withdraw at a word.
9-26: Zilu spent the night at Stone Gate.
9-27: 子擊磬於衛。有荷蕢而過孔氏之門者，曰：有心哉
The Master was playing the stone chimes in Wei. A man carrying a basket passed the gate of the Kong household and said: There is a heart in it!
9-28: 書云：高宗諒陰，三年不言
The Documents say, 'Gaozong, in the mourning hut, did not speak for three years.'
9-29: 子路問君子。子曰：修己以敬
Zilu asked about the gentleman. The Master said: He cultivates himself with reverence.
9-30: 原壤夷俟。子曰：幼而不孫弟，長而無述焉，老而……
Yuan Rang sat squatting, waiting. The Master said: Young, you were not humble or respectful to elders; grown, you accomplished nothing worth mentioning; old, you do not die — you are a pest!
10-1: A boy from Que village was carrying messages.
10-2: Duke Ling of Wei asked Confucius about military formations.
10-3: 賜也，女以予為多學而識之者與
Ci, do you think I am someone who has learned a great deal and remembers it all?
10-4: You, those who understand virtue are few.
10-5: 子張問行。子曰：言忠信，行篤敬，雖蠻貊之邦行……
Zizhang asked how to get along. The Master said: Let your words be loyal and true and your conduct sincere and reverent, and you will get along even among the barbarian states.
10-6: 直哉史魚！邦有道，如矢；邦無道，如矢
How upright Shi Yu is! When the state has the Way, he is like an arrow; when the state lacks the Way, he is like an arrow.
10-7: 可與言而不與之言，失人；不可與言而與之言，失……
Not to speak with someone you should speak with is to lose a person; to speak with someone you should not speak with is to waste words.
10-8: 子貢問為仁。子曰：工欲善其事，必先利其器
Zigong asked about practicing humaneness. The Master said: A craftsman who wants to do his work well must first sharpen his tools.
10-9: 顏淵問為邦。子曰：行夏之時，乘殷之輅，服周之……
Yan Yuan asked about governing a state. The Master said: Use the calendar of Xia, ride the carriage of Yin, wear the cap of Zhou…
10-10: One who does not think far ahead will surely have worries close at hand.
10-11: 已矣乎！吾未見好德如好色者也
It is hopeless! I have never seen anyone who loves virtue as much as he loves beauty.
10-12: 躬自厚而薄責於人，則遠怨矣
Demand much of yourself and little of others, and you will keep resentment far away.
10-13: 群居終日，言不及義，好行小慧，難矣哉
Those who gather all day long, whose talk never touches on what is right, and who love to show off petty cleverness — they are hard to deal with!
10-14: 君子病無能焉，不病人之不己知也
The gentleman is troubled by his own lack of ability, not by others' failure to know him.
10-15: 君子矜而不爭，群而不黨
The gentleman is dignified but does not contend; he is sociable but not partisan.
10-16: 有一言而可以終身行之者乎
Is there one word that one can practice all one's life?
10-17: In my dealings with people, whom have I disparaged, whom have I praised?
10-18: 巧言亂德，小不忍則亂大謀
Clever words confuse virtue. Lack of patience in small things ruins great plans.
10-19: 眾惡之，必察焉；眾好之，必察焉
When everyone hates someone, you must look into it; when everyone loves someone, you must look into it.
10-20: To err and not correct it — that is truly to err.
10-21: 吾嘗終日不食，終夜不寢，以思，無益，不如學也
I once went all day without eating and all night without sleeping in order to think. It was of no use. It is better to learn.
10-22: 知及之，仁不能守之；雖得之，必失之
If knowledge reaches it but humaneness cannot hold it, then even if he gains it, he is sure to lose it.
10-23: 君子不可小知，而可大受也；小人不可大受，而可……
The gentleman cannot be known through small things, but can be entrusted with great ones; the petty man cannot be entrusted with great things, but can be known through small ones.
10-24: The people need humaneness more than water and fire.
10-25: When it comes to humaneness, do not yield even to your teacher.
10-26: In teaching, there are no classes of people.
10-27: Music Master Mian came to see the Master. When he reached the steps, the Master said: Here are the steps.
10-28: The Ji family was about to attack Zhuanyu.
10-29: 天下有道，則禮樂征伐自天子出；天下無道，則禮……
When the realm has the Way, ritual, music, and punitive expeditions come from the Son of Heaven; when the realm lacks the Way, they come from the lords.
10-30: 祿之去公室，五世矣；政逮於大夫，四世矣；故夫……
It has been five generations since the revenues left the ducal house, and four since government passed to the ministers. That is why the descendants of the Three Huan are in decline.
10-31: There are three kinds of friends who help and three who harm.
11-1: There are three kinds of enjoyment that help and three that harm.
11-2: 侍於君子有三愆：言未及之而言謂之躁，言及之而……

In attending a gentleman there are three errors. To speak before it is your turn is called rashness; not to speak when it is your turn is called concealment; to speak without watching his expression is called blindness.
11-3: 君子有三戒：少之時，血氣未定，戒之在色；及其……

The gentleman guards against three things. In youth, when the blood and breath are not yet settled, he guards against lust. In his prime, when the blood and breath are strong, he guards against strife. In old age, when the blood and breath have declined, he guards against greed.
11-4: 君子有三畏：畏天命，畏大人，畏聖人之言
The gentleman holds three things in awe: the decree of Heaven, great men, and the words of the sages.
11-5: 生而知之者，上也；學而知之者，次也；困而學之……

Those born knowing are the highest; those who learn and come to know are next; those who learn when they meet difficulty are next again; those who meet difficulty and still do not learn — these people are the lowest.
11-6: 君子有九思：視思明，聽思聰，色思溫，貌思恭，……

The gentleman has nine things to think about: in seeing, to see clearly; in hearing, to hear keenly; in his expression, to be warm; in his bearing, to be respectful; in his words, to be loyal; in his work, to be reverent; in doubt, to ask; in anger, to think of the consequences; and when seeing gain, to think of what is right.
11-7: 見善如不及，見不善如探湯
Seeing good, act as if you could not reach it; seeing evil, act as if testing boiling water.
11-8: 齊景公有馬千駟，死之日，民無德而稱焉
Duke Jing of Qi had a thousand teams of four horses, yet on the day he died the people found no virtue in him to praise.
11-9: 陳亢問於伯魚曰：子亦有異聞乎
Chen Kang asked Boyu: Have you heard anything different from your father?
11-10: 邦君之妻，君稱之曰夫人，夫人自稱曰小童；邦人……

The wife of a ruler of a state: the ruler calls her 'Lady'; she calls herself 'little child'; the people of the state call her 'the ruler's Lady'; speaking of her to other states, they call her 'our little ruler'; people of other states also call her 'the ruler's Lady'.
11-11: 陽貨欲見孔子，孔子不見，歸孔子豚
Yang Huo wanted Confucius to come see him, but Confucius would not, so Yang Huo sent Confucius a pig.
11-12: By nature people are close to one another; by practice they grow far apart.
11-13: The Master went to Wucheng and heard the sound of strings and singing.
11-14: 公山弗擾以費畔，召，子欲往
Gongshan Furao held Bi in revolt and summoned the Master, and the Master wanted to go.
11-16: Bi Xi summoned the Master, and the Master wanted to go.
11-17: 由也，女聞六言六蔽矣乎
You, have you heard of the six words and their six flaws?
11-18: My young friends, why does none of you study the Odes?
11-19: 子謂伯魚曰：女為周南召南矣乎
The Master said to Boyu: Have you studied the Zhounan and Shaonan?
11-20: Ritual, they say, ritual — is it only jade and silk?
11-21: To hear something on the road and repeat it along the way is to throw virtue away.
11-22: Can one serve a ruler alongside a base man?
11-23: 古者民有三疾，今也或是之亡也
In ancient times, people had three failings; now perhaps even these are gone.
11-24: Clever words and an ingratiating look — seldom are they humane.
11-25: 予欲無言。子貢曰：子如不言，則小子何述焉
I would rather not speak. Zigong said: If you do not speak, Master, what will we disciples pass on?
11-26: 孺悲欲見孔子，孔子辭以疾
Ru Bei wanted to see Confucius; Confucius declined, pleading illness.
11-27: 食夫稻，衣夫錦，於女安乎
Eating that rice and wearing that brocade — would you be at ease?
11-28: 飽食終日，無所用心，難矣哉
To eat one's fill all day and give one's mind to nothing — that is hard indeed!
11-29: 君子尚勇乎？子曰：君子義以為上
Does the gentleman esteem courage? The Master said: The gentleman holds what is right as highest.
11-30: Does the gentleman also have things he hates?
12-1: 唯女子與小人為難養也，近之則不孫，遠之則怨
Women and petty men are the hardest to deal with. Keep them close and they become insolent; keep them at a distance and they resent it.
12-2: 微子去之，箕子為之奴，比干諫而死
The Viscount of Wei left, the Viscount of Ji became a slave, and Bi Gan remonstrated and died.
12-3: Liuxia Hui served as chief judge and was dismissed three times.
12-4: 齊景公待孔子，曰：若季氏則吾不能，以季、孟之……
Duke Jing of Qi, discussing how to treat Confucius, said: I cannot treat him as the Ji family is treated; I will treat him somewhere between the Ji and the Meng.
12-5: 楚狂接輿歌而過孔子曰：鳳兮
Jieyu, the madman of Chu, passed Confucius singing: Phoenix!
12-6: 長沮、桀溺耦而耕，孔子過之，使子路問津焉
Changju and Jieni were ploughing side by side. Confucius passed by and sent Zilu to ask them where the ford was.
12-7: 子路從而後，遇丈人，以杖荷蓧
Zilu, following the Master, fell behind and met an old man carrying a basket on his staff.
12-8: 不降其志，不辱其身，伯夷、叔齊與
Not lowering their aims nor disgracing themselves — that was Boyi and Shuqi.
12-9: 大師摯適齊，亞飯干適楚，三飯繚適蔡，四飯缺適……
Grand Music Master Zhi went to Qi; Gan, master of the second meal, went to Chu; Liao, master of the third meal, went to Cai; Que, master of the fourth meal, went to Qin.
12-10: 周公謂魯公曰：君子不施其親
The Duke of Zhou said to the Duke of Lu: The gentleman does not neglect his kin.
12-11: 周有八士：伯達、伯適、仲突、仲忽、叔夜、叔夏……
Zhou had eight scholars: Boda, Bokuo, Zhongtu, Zhonghu, Shuye, Shuxia, Jisui, and Jigua.
12-12: 士見危致命，見得思義，祭思敬，喪思哀，其可已……
A scholar who, seeing danger, offers his life; seeing gain, thinks of what is right; at sacrifices, thinks of reverence; in mourning, thinks of grief — such a one will do.
12-13: 子夏之門人問交於子張
Zixia's disciples asked Zizhang about making friends.
12-14: 雖小道，必有可觀者焉；致遠恐泥，是以君子不為……
Even minor arts surely have something worth seeing; but if pursued far, one fears getting bogged down. That is why the gentleman does not pursue them.
12-15: 博學而篤志，切問而近思，仁在其中矣
Learn broadly and keep your aims firm; ask earnestly and reflect on what is close at hand. Humaneness lies in this.
12-16: 百工居肆以成其事，君子學以致其道
The hundred artisans stay in their workshops to complete their work; the gentleman learns in order to reach his Way.
12-17: 君子信而後勞其民，未信則以為厲己也；信而後諫……

The gentleman wins the trust of his people before he works them; without their trust, they will think he is oppressing them. He wins trust before he remonstrates; without trust, the ruler will think he is slandering him.
12-18: 子夏之門人小子，當灑掃、應對、進退，則可矣
Zixia's disciples and young followers are fine when it comes to sprinkling and sweeping, answering and responding, coming forward and withdrawing.
12-19: 仕而優則學，學而優則仕
When one in office has energy to spare, he should learn; when one who learns has energy to spare, he should take office.
12-20: 堂堂乎張也，難與並為仁矣
How imposing Zhang is! It is hard to practice humaneness alongside him.
12-21: 吾聞諸夫子：孟莊子之孝也，其他可能也；其不改……

I have heard from the Master: As for the filial piety of Meng Zhuangzi, the rest of it others could manage; but his not changing his father's ministers or his father's policies — that is hard to manage.
12-22: 孟氏使陽膚為士師，問於曾子
The Meng family made Yang Fu chief judge, and he asked Zengzi for advice.
12-23: 紂之不善，不如是之甚也
Zhou's wickedness was not as extreme as they say.
12-24: 君子之過也，如日月之食焉：過也，人皆見之；更……
The faults of the gentleman are like eclipses of the sun and moon. When he errs, everyone sees it; when he corrects it, everyone looks up to him.
12-25: 衛公孫朝問於子貢曰：仲尼焉學
Gongsun Chao of Wei asked Zigong: From whom did Zhongni learn?
12-26: 叔孫武叔語大夫於朝，曰：子貢賢於仲尼
Shusun Wushu said to the ministers at court: Zigong is worthier than Zhongni.
12-28: 陳子禽謂子貢曰：子為恭也，仲尼豈賢於子乎
Chen Ziqin said to Zigong: You are just being modest. How could Zhongni be worthier than you?
12-29: 諮！爾舜！天之歷數在爾躬
Ah, you, Shun! The succession ordained by Heaven rests in your person.
12-30: 子張問於孔子曰：何如斯可以從政矣
Zizhang asked Confucius: What must one do to take part in government?
12-31: Without knowing fate, one cannot be a gentleman.
